headline: Post-election relief rally cools as chip-specific weakness creeps in
body: Wednesday's session was the story: the Dow surged roughly 3% to its best day in well over a year as midterm election results cleared a slice of political uncertainty, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posting strong, broad gains (advancers outpacing decliners by about 3-to-1) and oil tumbling more than 8% as geopolitical risk eased. That relief rally is cooling into today's session rather than extending: Dow futures are only modestly higher, S&P futures are roughly flat, and the Nasdaq is the laggard, pressured by a chip-sector stumble after a major mobile-chip supplier's soft sales outlook knocked its stock down double digits premarket and dragged peers lower. Oil is only partially retracing Wednesday's drop, and commentary continues to flag lingering Middle East tension as an unresolved overhang rather than a closed story.

Underneath the price action, positioning data suggests the rally hasn't fully won converts: the latest AAII individual-investor survey showed bearish responses near 41%, well above its historical average of roughly 32%, even as bullish responses sat close to their own average — a split pointing to lingering skepticism rather than broad conviction chasing the move higher. Retail chatter on forums like WallStreetBets and Stocktwits didn't turn up a clear, fresh signal for today specifically, so this read leans more on price action and survey positioning than on social-media sentiment. Taken together, the setup looks like a market reacting to a specific political catalyst and a chip-sector guidance miss, with the broader crowd still more cautious than the week's headline gains would suggest.
